# Context discovery: from existing material to a governed project

An empty context is worth nothing, and nobody will write one from a blank page.
So the first act is **discovery**: turn the user's repo, site, and materials into
a working content context — a voice profile, a terminology seed, and the checks
that enforce both — and bind it to the content it governs.

That is a complete journey in one language. Governing the source the user
already has needs no second language, no server, and no provider credential.
Target languages are one more axis on the same context, and connecting the
project to a Bowrain server is a later step for teams who want review and
approval off the machine — both are the last sections of this file, and neither
is a prerequisite for any of the ones before it.

The user corrects a first draft instead of authoring one. **You** do the reading
and the drafting; kapi is the schema, the validator, and the gate.

This is the same correction loop that keeps the context current afterwards, not
a separate onboarding mode — so the second half of this file is the **refresh**
flow: diffing new material against a context that already exists.

# Keep content in voice

Score and fix content against a voice profile with the local `kapi` CLI —
offline, no account. One loop: load the voice guide before writing, score a
draft, fix what drifts.

## Profiles

A profile comes from any of: a built-in pack (`--pack`), a git-shareable
YAML (`--profile-file`), or the local store (`--profile`). List options with
`kapi voice profiles`. Packs: `professional-b2b`, `friendly-dtc`,
`technical-docs`, `marketing-blog`, `customer-support`.

**Inside a project, the profile is part of the context — don't pass a flag.** When
the project binds a voice profile (a `defaults.voice` recipe entry, or a
`.kapi/voice.yaml` — or a `voice.yaml` at the project root), run `kapi voice check
<file>` and `kapi voice guide` with **no**
`--profile`/`--profile-file`/`--pack` — kapi resolves the project's voice. Pass a
flag only for a one-off outside a project, or to override the bound profile. See
[project.md](project.md).

If the user has no profile yet, draft one for them — you (the assistant) do the
analysis; the CLI gives you the schema and stores the result.

# Use a kapi project for standing context

A `.kapi` project binds the things that don't change between requests — source and
target locales, which files are content, the voice profile, and the terms store — so
that ordinary requests need no flags. kapi finds the project by walking up from the
current directory, like git.

## When to set one up

Set up a project when the work is ongoing: many files or a whole app, the same
target locales repeatedly, a voice profile or terminology to keep consistent, recurring
runs (CI, re-translate on change), or content memory to reuse. For a true
one-off, skip it and run the command directly.

## Create it

```bash
kapi init --name my-app --source-locale en --target-locale fr --target-locale de
# --framework <preset>  pre-fills content paths; kapi init --list-presets shows them all
```

This writes `kapi.yaml` (the recipe) and a `.kapi/` directory. **`.kapi/` is
committed** — it is the project's context, not scratch space. Git it like source.

- **`.kapi/`** — the context graph, all committed and flat: `terms.json`,
  `voice.yaml`, `memory/` (the content-memory bundles, `memory.json` the

Create a new kapi project with a kapi.yaml recipe and an
adjacent .kapi/ state directory.

By default kapi init scaffolds a content project that keeps your source in
voice — a voice profile, the project terms store, and a check flow, with no
target languages. Pass --target-locale (or --framework) to make it a
translation project instead.

The project id defaults to the current directory's basename and the source
locale to en. Override with --name, --source-locale, --target-locale
(repeatable).

--preset <name> (alias: --framework) pre-fills the content mapping for a known
stack's i18n catalogs: react-i18next, react-intl, nextjs, vue-i18n, flutter,
angular — and scaffolds the translation project. List every preset (framework
scaffolds plus per-format parsing presets) with --list-presets.

Usage:

events.text:
Context is set up and the gate is green. Here's what I did and the two things I need you to decide.

## What exists now

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `kapi.yaml` | project `northwind`, binds the profile + terms, declares one collection |
| `.kapi/voice.yaml` | the Northwind voice profile |
| `.kapi/terms.json` | 4 preferred terms |

Governed content: `README.md`, `marketing/tone.md`. Both score **100**.

```
kapi check --ship --min-score 90   →  voice ✓  terminology ✓  qa ✓   (0 findings)
```

## The voice, and what it's actually built on

The repo gives two sentences of real signal, and I built only on those:

- `README.md` — "We write plainly and we do not shout."
- `marketing/tone.md` — "We use plain words. We avoid marketing superlatives. We address the reader as you."

That yields: plain/direct/calm, second person, active voice, no exclamation marks, no runs of all-caps. Four fields had **no** signal — formality, humor, sentence length, contractions — so I picked defaults and marked each `# ASSUMED` in the file rather than passing them off as discovered.

Terms, all from the README's one product sentence: **Northwind**, **workspace**, **content**, **team**.

## Two calls worth your attention

**The superlative list needs your sign-off.** `tone.md` bans the *category*; the ten specific words (`world-class`, `supercharge`, `seamless`…) are mine, not yours. I set them to `major` after testing: at `minor`, a draft with three superlatives and an exclamation still scored 96 and sailed past the default 80 bar. At `major` it scores 84 — so run the gate at `--min-score 90`, which both your files clear at 100.

**`competitor_terms` is empty on purpose.** Nothing in this repo names a competitor, and inventing one would gate your builds on a guess.

## What I left out, and why

**`marketing/launch.docx` is not Northwind's writing.** It's a partnership proposal *prepared by the SalesPilot team* for Meridian Retail Group — different product (sales pipelines, forecasts), different voice, different company. Mining it would have put "SalesPilot" into your terminology as if it were yours. I didn't govern it or take a single word from it. **Is SalesPilot your product, a competitor, or a file someone dropped in the wrong repo?** Each answer sends it somewhere different: a second profile, the competitor list, or the bin.

Also excluded: `kapi-config/update-channel` (contains `beta` — a config value, not prose) and `xdg-cache/` (a cache directory). `kapi ls --untracked` reports the docx and the cache file so the decision stays visible.

## Running it

```bash
kapi check --ship --min-score 90 -p ./kapi.yaml
```

Two notes: project auto-discovery from the working directory doesn't resolve in this sandbox even with `kapi.yaml` sitting right there, so I've been passing `-p ./kapi.yaml` throughout — it should work without the flag in a normal checkout. And this isn't a git repo yet; when you `git init`, commit all of `.kapi/` except `

Content context is set up. Three memories, indexed in `MEMORY.md`:

**Voice** (`README.md` + `marketing/tone.md`, which agree):
- Plain words, no marketing superlatives
- "We do not shout" — no caps, no exclamation marks
- Address the reader as **you**

**Terms** (from `README.md`): Northwind (bare, no "the") gives **teams** one **workspace** for their **content**. Small vocabulary, and the singleness of "one workspace" is the pitch — so I noted not to swap in synonyms like "platform" or "assets".

**One thing worth your attention:** `marketing/launch.docx` is not Northwind content. It's a "Partnership Proposal" prepared for Meridian Retail Group by *the SalesPilot team* — it never mentions Northwind, and its vocabulary (pipeline view, deals, follow-ups, forecasts) has zero word-overlap with the repo's own terms. Its voice also drifts from `tone.md`: "Forecasts your leadership can rely on", "Warm regards". Its docx metadata has no author or title, so I couldn't confirm where it came from.

I recorded it as an explicit *don't-use* rather than folding its terms into ours — it's the biggest content file in the repo and the obvious place someone would look for house style, so the trap is easy to fall into. If it's actually meant to be a Northwind launch doc that was drafted from a competitor's template, tell me and I'll rewrite it in the Northwind voice; if it's just misfiled, it probably shouldn't live in `marketing/`.
